# TITLE LINUX SECURITY HANDBOOK # SUBTITLE 2. USERS, GROUPS, AND IDENTITY SECURITY # BADGES PAGE 2 OF 20 # SECTION_HEADINGS - LOCAL USERS AND SYSTEM ACCOUNTS - /ETC/PASSWD - /ETC/SHADOW - /ETC/GROUP - UID AND GID SECURITY - DETECTING UNEXPECTED ACCOUNTS - LOCKING AND DISABLING ACCOUNTS - REVIEWING PRIVILEGED USERS - KEY MANAGEMENT COMMANDS - KEY ACCOUNT FILES - KEY COMMANDS # BODY_PARAGRAPHS **LOCAL USERS AND SYSTEM ACCOUNTS** Linux uses local users and system accounts to manage access and ownership. System accounts usually have low UIDs and no login shell. **/ETC/PASSWD** Stores user account information including username, UID, GID, home directory, and default shell. **/ETC/SHADOW** Stores encrypted passwords and password aging information. Access is restricted to the root user. **/ETC/GROUP** Stores group information including GID and member list. **UID AND GID SECURITY** Every user and group has a unique UID and GID. Protect UID 0 (root) and other privileged IDs. **DETECTING UNEXPECTED ACCOUNTS** Regularly check for unknown or suspicious user accounts and groups. **LOCKING AND DISABLING ACCOUNTS** Lock or disable unused or compromised accounts to prevent unauthorized access. **REVIEWING PRIVILEGED USERS** Review users with UID 0 and sudo access. Limit privileged access to only what is necessary. **KEY MANAGEMENT COMMANDS** Use Linux commands to inspect and manage users, groups, and account settings. These files are critical for identity security. Protect them carefully. # IMPORTANT_FILES | File Path | Description | | :--- | :--- | | /etc/passwd | User account information | | /etc/shadow | Encrypted passwords and aging info | | /etc/group | Group information and members | # TABLES ## Main Content Table (Rows) | Icon/Header | Content | | :--- | :--- | | **LOCAL USERS AND SYSTEM ACCOUNTS** | Linux uses local users and system accounts to manage access and ownership.
